criteria.criterion: The CAS-mismatch branch logs the git stderr (and the ref + expected oid) before raising, at a level that survives into CI logs — so the next occurrence is diagnosable.

On LeaseLostError, the holder additionally records what the remote ref actually was (e.g. an ls-remote of the lock ref plus the holder recorded in the lock blob), so 'stolen by whom' is answerable rather than inferred.

The marker set no longer classifies non-CAS rejections (hook decline, server ref-lock contention, rate limit, internal error) as a lease mismatch, with a unit test driving the real stderr shapes above and asserting the split.
Fail-closed behaviour for genuine transport failures (auth, DNS) is unchanged and still covered.
